dedupe_keys.name: topotherm district heating network design optimisation

description: topotherm is an open Pyomo-based mixed-integer linear programming model for designing district heating networks that scales to large districts for single and multiple time steps. It is developed by Jerry Lambert and Amedeo Ceruti at the Chair of Energy Systems of the Technical University of Munich, with releases up to 0.6.0. It was introduced in a 2024 paper in Energy that benchmarks four open formulations (Résimont, DHmin, DHNx and topotherm) on synthetic cases and real urban districts with up to 9,587 potential edges, where topotherm solved fastest for single time steps; the benchmark code is archived on Zenodo. It imports and exports GIS files and works with Gurobi or open-source solvers. Coverage is not tied to a place. The code is accessible on GitHub under the MIT licence at no cost. Caveats: large cases benefit from a commercial solver, and results depend on demand and cost inputs. Simulation uses are district heating network routing and sizing for heat planning. Related records: model-dhnx is one of the benchmarked models, and data-district-heating-long-term-unit-commitment-instances gives district heating optimisation instances.
inputs: GIS files of streets, buildings and heat sources
name: topotherm - district heating network design optimisation
